# 17 Titanic — voicing round (Batch 2A, weight and space)

*Generated by tests/voicing/batch02a.py. Level reading: RMS over +6..+10 s of the A1 hold (phrase f); matched to the bank reference (−18.0 dBFS RMS) by VOLUME; phrase (b)'s reading is in the table too. Every change is before → after under the echo rule. WAVs are on the listen/batch-02a-weight-and-space branch only.*

**Recommended: B centre** — dual saws a fifth apart (OSC 2 +7 st, both at full level) in a DUAL pair about 5.5 cents apart, cold (no drive, RESO 12, no effects) and heavy, with an extreme bass compensation: KEY TRK 12 (9 %), so the filter opens for low notes and closes for high ones. The same note struck at A1 / A2 / A3 puts 8.4 / 5.5 / 3.4 harmonics under the centroid (A: 5.3 / 4.1 / 3.1) and A1 is 0.6 dB louder than A3; the stack is 30 % under 60 Hz, 43 % in 60-150 Hz (the fifth lives there), only 5 % above 400 Hz: freezing and desolate rather than bright. It reads -17.9 dBFS on the steady hold and -17.1 on phrase (b) (difference +0.8 dB), releases in 1300 ms to -60 dB, and costs 1594 worst-case host instr/sample (idle 104 + load 1490). C is the same patch colder and darker (5.9 harmonics at A1, centroid 294 Hz against B's 421, release 3036 ms); D adds the tape weather (2371 worst-case host instr/sample (idle 866 + load 1506)).

## What to listen to

`*_slow.wav` (A1 held 10 s then let go: the weight, the beat of the pair, the release), `*_riff.wav` (A1-A2 chopped: the bass compensation, the long release against the chop)
and `*_stabs.wav` (fifth-and-octave chords: the DUAL pair, POLY 6). Listen for: cold or just dull (B against C), whether the fifth is a hollow power chord or a hum, whether the low
notes open up and the high ones close down the way an anchor should, and whether D's tape weather is a garnish or a distraction.
